title: Gujarat-Born Scientist Karim Maredia Wins Borlaug CAST Communication Award
excerpt: The Michigan State University professor and dairy farmer's son from rural Gujarat has spent 35 years bridging agricultural science with communities across 60 countries.
body:
• Dr. Karimbhai M. Maredia, professor and director of the World Agriculture Center at Michigan State University, has been named the 2026 recipient of the Borlaug CAST Communication Award.
  • Born in a small village in Gujarat to a dairy farming family, Maredia has spent more than 35 years building science communication programs across 60-plus countries.
  • The award will be presented on December 10 at the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C.
  • Maredia has trained over 15,000 professionals, hosted 250 visiting scholars, and secured more than $55 million in competitive grants during his career at MSU.

The Council for Agricultural Science and Technology has named Dr. Karimbhai M. Maredia, a professor, associate dean and director of the World Agriculture Center at Michigan State University's College of Agriculture and Natural Resources, as the 2026 recipient of the Borlaug CAST Communication Award.

The award, named after Nobel Peace Prize laureate Norman E. Borlaug — widely known as the father of the Green Revolution — recognises scientists who effectively communicate agricultural science and technology to non-technical audiences. Maredia will receive the honour at a ceremony on December 10 at the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C.

From Gujarat Village to Global Platform

Maredia's story begins in a small village in Gujarat, where he grew up as the son of a local dairy farmer. His early roots in rural India shaped his belief that scientific knowledge must serve broader society, according to American Bazaar.

https://x.com/DeccanHerald/status/2097210446835003500

He earned a Bachelor of Science in Agriculture from Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth in India before moving to the United States for graduate studies. He completed a Master of Science in Integrated Pest Management at Alabama A&M University and a Ph.D. in Plant Breeding and Integrated Pest Management from the University of Arkansas.

Following his doctoral work, Maredia served from 1986 to 1989 as a postdoctoral fellow and research scientist at the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center in Mexico — the same research institute where Borlaug himself conducted his Green Revolution wheat breeding work.

Three Decades at Michigan State

Maredia joined MSU in 1989 and has spent more than 35 years building one of the most far-reaching science communication programs in international agriculture. As director of WorldTAP — the World Knowledge and Technology Access Program — he has travelled to more than 60 countries, working to bring research, technology and innovation directly to farmers, scientists and policymakers.

“The award celebrates not only my individual efforts but also the enduring power of partnerships, collaborations, and shared vision across national and international boundaries.”

— Dr. Karim Maredia

The numbers behind his career are substantial. Maredia has trained over 15,000 professionals from 80 countries, hosted 250 visiting scholars, authored or edited 130 publications including eight co-edited books on integrated pest management and agricultural extension, and secured more than $55 million in competitive grants, according to American Bazaar. His work has been supported by USAID, USDA, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, the World Bank, the Rockefeller Foundation, Winrock International and the Gates Foundation.

Continuing Ties to India

Despite building his career in the United States, Maredia has maintained direct engagement with Indian agricultural governance. He currently serves as Foreign Secretary of the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences of India, underscoring his role as a bridge between American agricultural research and Indian farming communities.

“The Borlaug CAST Communication Award exists for scientists like Karim Maredia — people who believe that research only fulfils its promise when it reaches the people it was meant to serve,” said Chris Boomsma, CAST CEO, according to High Plains Journal. “His career is a masterclass in what science communication looks like when it is done right, at scale, and across borders.”

What's Next

The December 10 ceremony at the Library of Congress will honour Maredia alongside other leaders in agricultural science communication. For the diaspora community, his recognition adds to a growing list of Indian-origin scientists making their mark in American institutions while maintaining deep connections to their roots in India.
